info.name: woo-request-scoped-access — a Woo request's assessments are private to the people on it
info.description:
woo-request-scoped-access tasks 1.2, 2.3 (through the caller) and 3.3. Folder `private` proves REQ-WSA-001: the shipped wooDocumentAssessment schema carries authorization.scope private, and a colleague who is on the case neither as handler nor as reviewer lists none of its assessments and cannot read one by uuid. Folder `ownership` proves REQ-WSA-003: a second reviewer's verdict on an assessment the handler made is refused through the case route and through the OpenRegister object API, the verdict stays, and a coordinator (dossiq-coordinators, the Woo case type's reviewerAccess.supervisorGroup) changes it. Folder `reassign` proves REQ-WSA-005: the handler cannot hand the case on (reassign-needs-supervisor), a coordinator can, and the former handler then reads no assessment. Setup provisions four accounts (handler, batch reviewer, unassigned colleague, coordinator) and a throwaway Woo case of the seeded Woo case type with two in-scope documents; teardown removes them. Who is a reviewer follows tests/e2e/woo-blind-review.spec.ts: the handler assesses, the second reviewer holds a review batch and a read share on the case.

@newman exclude Runs on the live pass through tests/newman/run-all.sh (decision 139): it provisions accounts and needs the seeded Woo case type and OpenRegister's private scope and per-object grants, which the CI newman job (enable-newman false, newman-collection-path 'data') does not set up. See the comment on enable-newman in .github/workflows/code-quality.yml.
